note: One drill, a tune built on a leap down, in two sizes: a fall of a 4th, then a drop of an octave, each learned in the named stages (with the tune, Tune muted over the chords, Chords muted too), then a tune of the singer's own over a drone with one of those leaps in it. The key is moves, with a {{?key}} line on what stays the same.

exercise.title: Tunes that fall a 4th and an octave
exercise.why: A fall of a 4th from Fa and a drop of an octave from the high Do both land on Do, so keep the sound of Do in your ear and the leap has somewhere known to land.

cells.text:
Press Play below to hear the tune: the mic starts with it. The tune starts on Fa and falls a 4th to Do. Sing along on the note names.
Sing along with the tune a few times. Then press Tune below to mute the tune, and sing it over the chords alone.
Once the fall lands without a slide, press Chords to mute the chords too, and sing the tune a cappella.

Press Play below to hear the tune: the mic starts with it. This tune starts on the high Do and drops an octave to Do. Sing along on the note names.
Sing along with the tune a few times. Then press Tune below to mute the tune, and sing it over the chords alone.
Once the drop lands without a slide, press Chords to mute the chords too, and sing the tune a cappella.
{{?key}}In another key the notes are new, and the falls are still a 4th and an octave.

Press Start exercise below: the drone and the mic start together. Make up a short tune from the notes on the staff with one leap down in it, a 4th or an octave, and end on {{1}}. Sing it on "la".
Then make another that starts with the leap, from {{4}} down to {{1}} or from the high {{1}} down to the low one.
